answer.label: Not Bob Marley — an unsourced modern paraphrase
answer.authorDates: Attributed name: Bob Marley, 1945–1981 · Jamaican reggae singer-songwriter
answer.sourceLine: There is no documented Marley source — no song lyric, interview, letter, or writing — that contains this line. Wikiquote records it only among “Unsourced” attributions ↗, noting it surfaced recently and does not match his voice. Treat it as an anonymous inspirational line pinned on a famous name, not something Marley is known to have said or written.

author.name: Bob Marley
author.heading: About the credited author
author.bio: Bob Marley (1945–1981) was a Jamaican singer, songwriter, and guitarist who became the global face of reggae and a symbol of resistance, unity, and Rastafarian spirituality. His documented words live in his lyrics and interviews — which is precisely why undated, sourceless “quotes” like this one, absent from that record, should be treated with caution.

cite.sourceCitation: No primary source located. Earliest documented attributions appear on quote-aggregation sites and social media; Wikipedia’s sister project Wikiquote lists the line under “Unsourced” on Talk:Bob Marley (accessed 2026).

misattribution.heading: Why this is pinned on Bob Marley
misattribution.intro: Bob Marley is one of the internet’s biggest magnets for feel-good, uplift-flavored quotes. Warm lines about integrity and character get captioned over his image and spread by quote sites, even when nothing ties them to his actual songs, interviews, or writing.

items.why: No Marley song lyric, interview transcript, letter, or book has been shown to contain it. Wikiquote files it as “Unsourced” ↗ and flags that it surfaced recently and does not sound like him.

items.who: Other quotes wrongly credited to Marley
items.why: Marley’s Wikiquote page keeps a Misattributed section ↗ — e.g. the “You will never find justice in a world where criminals make the rules” and “the people who are trying to make this world worse…” lines (the latter from the 2007 film I Am Legend) — showing how routinely inspirational text is falsely tagged to him.

misattribution.truthLine: Best evidence: this is an anonymous modern inspirational line with no verifiable Marley source — Wikiquote lists it as unsourced ↗, and no primary Marley work has been found to contain it.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentiment is appealing and on-brand for an idealist icon — greatness measured by integrity and positive influence rather than money — which is exactly why it travels well as a caption. But appeal is not attribution. The test for a Marley quote is a documented source: a lyric, an interview, a filmed or printed statement. This line has none.
Until someone produces a primary Marley source, the honest label is “unsourced.” It functions as anonymous motivational text that borrowed Marley’s name for reach.
context.pull: A warm sentiment, a famous face, and no source in between.
